Description: Improve an existing plan by getting an agent to expand on the details and implementation ideas.

content: Honor current user authorization, role ownership, and flow phase throughout; narrower read-only, no-planning-artifact, and no-commit instructions override command defaults. Research only identified decision-relevant unknowns, using established evidence before additional tool calls; external documentation is for relevant unresolved version/API/contract questions. Within those bounds, read `codeInfoStatus/flow-state/current-plan.json` first and determine the active `plan_path`, then extract repository paths from `additional_repositories` for this flow. If the handoff does not explicitly identify any additional repositories, treat that as none. The current repository is the canonical plan host and is implicitly in scope for authorized plan work only. If it also appears inside `additional_repositories`, treat that as redundant and ignore that entry. Verify that the selected plan file exists in the current repository, that the story number in the current repository branch name matches the story number in the selected plan filename, and that every additional repository is either already on a branch whose story number matches the selected plan filename or can safely create or reuse such a branch without overwriting local changes. If those do not match, stop and say the current-plan handoff is stale and must be regenerated. Do not independently search for or select a different plan. Read the plan's `Additional Repositories` section, supporting both `## Additional Repositories` and `### Additional Repositories`, and ensure it stays in sync with the repository names used by the tasks. Require explicit current user or agreed story scope before introducing work in another repository; adding a repository to the plan does not authorize it. After authorization, keep the plan's `Additional Repositories` section in sync. Without tasking up, is there any acceptance in this selected story plan that is not defined in a way that a junior developer could understand what the output should be? If so, please update all relevant planning sections to get them to where we need to be. For plan structure and formatting, honor current user instructions and the target repository's contract. Look for `plan_format.md` locally, then use code_info to locate a candidate in `codeInfo2` if needed. If no applicable contract is available, preserve the selected story's structure; borrow another repository's layout only after verifying compatibility, without importing requirements. Report uncertainty that affects the decision. Apply only evidenced necessary clarifications, preserving agreed acceptance criteria, exclusions, and goals. For unresolved material decisions, do focused research or report the affected change as blocked; ask only the needed question when a human is available. In unattended or no-questions work, do not guess. Commit only actual authorized changes when the current assignment permits commits; no changes is valid, and read-only/no-commit instructions override this default.

If the selected story requires coordinated changes across more than one ingested repository, you MUST treat it as a multi-repository story. In that case, update the plan so it explicitly states which repository each planned change belongs to throughout the story. Do not leave repository ownership implicit. At minimum, ensure the Description, Acceptance Criteria, Implementation Ideas, Message Contracts and Storage Shapes, Edge Cases and Failure Modes, tasks, subtasks, testing steps, and final validation clearly indicate the target repository or repositories for the work being described. Where one repository provides a library, API, shared type, message contract, or other dependency used by another repository, document the dependency direction, required sequencing, and any compatibility or migration expectations explicitly. If the story only affects one repository, do NOT add unnecessary multi-repository structure; keep the plan simple and use the normal single-repository style.
